Concrete Pool Decks · Longboat Key, FL

Concrete Pool Deck Installation on Longboat Key

A concrete pool deck on Longboat Key runs $5–$15 per sq ft installed as of October 2026. A deck on a Gulf-front lot can cross Florida's Coastal Construction Control Line, which brings in a state permit and the Town's own sea-turtle lighting review before the concrete gets priced.

By the Opera Concrete & Pavers estimating team · Updated October 1, 2026

What the Coastal Construction Control Line adds to a Gulf-front deck

Longboat Key's own site-plan rule flags the overlap directly, requiring a project to note any "FDEP Coastal Construction Control Line permit" it needs on top of the Town's own sign-off Longboat Key Code §158.030 Performance standards (open space, CCCL). The CCCL program exists to keep a private pool deck or patio from undercutting a dune or blocking public beach access, and DEP's own application process runs on its own schedule, separate from when the Town clears the zoning exception FDEP's CCCL program FDEP's CCCL application page.

Why the Pool Excavation Itself Is the Best Soil Test You'll Get

A pool excavation digs deeper into the ground than almost any other part of a Longboat Key project, which makes it the clearest look at actual soil conditions anyone on the job gets before the deck base goes in. If the hole hits standing water or visibly wet soil shallower than the published range for the area's dominant soil series suggests, we treat the deck base around that side of the pool as wet-soil work and add the extra 2 to 4 inches ICPI calls for, rather than assuming one soil reading applies evenly on every side of the same excavation.

Why deck lighting answers to a sea-turtle rule, not just the slab

New development seaward of the control line also pulls in Chapter 100's sea-turtle lighting review, which looks specifically at fixtures visible from the beach, pool-area sconces and deck lights included Longboat Key Code §100.04. A deck light aimed out toward the Gulf, or an uncovered pool-equipment light, is the kind of detail that can hold up a final inspection longer than the concrete pour itself, so we plan fixture placement against that rule before the deck's layout is finished.

Wire Mesh Does the Same Job Here It Does in a Driveway

Wire mesh in a pool deck slab doesn't stop cracking, the same as in any other flatwork, it holds the two sides of a crack together once one forms so they don't separate or lift under foot. That matters more right at the coping than it does in the middle of an open yard, since a crack allowed to widen near the pool edge can eventually undermine the coping's support. A Longboat Key deck built with mesh carried through to within a few inches of the isolation joint, rather than stopped short of it, keeps that particular crack risk lower without changing the joint layout at all.

Say you have a 28 × 30 ft pool deck, 840 sq ft, around a cage on a lot close enough to the Gulf to cross the control line

Say you have a 28 × 30 ft pool deck, 840 sq ft, around a cage on a lot close enough to the Gulf to cross the control line. At the market range of $5–$15 per sq ft, that runs $4,200 to $12,600, narrowing to roughly $5,880 to $10,080 in the typical $7–$12 band for a textured, slip-resistant finish pitched to a drain. Because part of the deck sits seaward of the CCCL, the state permit question gets answered before the Town's zoning exception is even relevant, and any deck or equipment lighting fixture gets checked against the sea-turtle rule rather than finalized by habit.

Applying the Kool Deck-Style Coating After the Base Cures

A spray texture coating doesn't go on the same day as the base slab pour, it waits until the concrete underneath has cured enough to take the topping without trapping moisture or causing bond problems. On a Longboat Key job, that usually means a gap of at least several days between the structural pour and the coating step, timed around the same curing standard as the base slab rather than rushed to finish sooner. Skipping ahead on that timeline is one of the more common reasons a coating delaminates or blisters within the first season, since it never had a fully cured, dry surface to bond to.

Slip Risk Where the Deck Stays Wet Longest

The section of deck closest to the pool, and any shaded strip under a lanai roof or a stand of trees, stays damp longer after each swim session or rain than the open sun-facing side, and that combination of standing moisture and algae film is where most slip incidents on a pool deck actually happen. A smooth or heavily sealed finish makes that worse, since sealing can fill in the texture a broom finish or acrylic coating was supposed to provide. On a Longboat Key deck, the shaded or splash-zone sections are worth checking for a slick film more often than the rest of the surface, since they develop the problem faster and show it less obviously.

Keeping the Equipment Pad Clear and Draining

The small slab under the pump, filter and heater needs the same basic upkeep as the rest of the deck, mainly keeping its control joint clear and confirming water still drains away from the equipment rather than pooling at its base after a storm. A Longboat Key homeowner doing routine pool maintenance is usually standing right at that pad anyway, so a quick look at the slab under the equipment costs nothing extra and catches a drainage problem before it reaches anything electrical. Landscaping or mulch added near the pad over the years can quietly redirect water back toward it even when the original grading was correct.

Frequently asked questions

Does my Longboat Key pool deck need a state permit as well as a Town one?

If it crosses Florida's Coastal Construction Control Line, yes, a DEP permit is required, and the Town's own site-plan rule requires that permit to be noted before its own sign-off is relevant.

Does pool deck lighting need special approval near the Gulf?

New development seaward of the control line pulls in the Town's sea-turtle lighting review under Chapter 100, which looks at fixtures visible from the beach, including pool and deck lights.

Is my Longboat Key lot in a flood zone that affects the deck?

Possibly. On FEMA's coastal maps, Zone AE carries a lighter wave hazard than the Coastal High Hazard Zone VE, where surf is strong enough to damage an unreinforced deck edge during a major storm; the dividing line can split a single block.
